overview: A feature-heavy week on bpf-next with several large series under active review. Yonghong Song's 20-patch series enabling exception cleanup landing pads for bpf_throw() reached v3, providing proper C++ destructor semantics during BPF exception unwinding. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi's 11-patch series fixing __uninit kfunc output buffer handling in the verifier reached v5. Kuniyuki Iwashima posted a 7-patch series adding bpf_tcp_ops hooks for TCP AutoLOWAT, and Anastasios Papagiannis landed v9 of the mm_struct user-memory kfuncs series. Hash map memory and performance improvements from T.J. Mercier and Mykyta Yatsenko also progressed this week.

patches.title: bpf: Accept the compiler's exception cleanup table at program load
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: First patch of a 20-patch v3 series implementing exception cleanup landing pads for bpf_throw(). The series teaches the BPF loader to accept a compiler-generated .bpf_cleanup section, adds bpf_unwind_resume() as a new kfunc, wires landing pads into the verifier's CFG walk, and adds JIT support on x86 and arm64. This enables BPF programs compiled with C++ exception semantics to run proper destructors when bpf_throw() unwinds the stack, a major step toward full exception-handling support in BPF.

patches.title: bpf: Fix generic __uninit kfunc output buffers
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Core fix in an 11-patch v5 series addressing incorrect verifier handling of kfunc __uninit output arguments. The series corrects the verifier to treat such arguments as write-only, supports multiple __uninit outputs per kfunc call, preserves stack initialization for generic output buffers, and validates read access for helper input/output buffers. Together these changes close several verifier loopholes related to uninitialized memory in kfunc calls.

patches.title: bpf: Add user memory access kfuncs for mm_struct
patches.author: Anastasios Papagiannis
patches.summary: Third patch of a 5-patch v9 series adding kfuncs that allow BPF programs to read user-space memory strings via a process's mm_struct, without requiring a BPF program to run in the context of that process. The series introduces copy_remote_mm_str() in the mm layer, marks linux_binprm->mm as trusted-or-null for the verifier, and wires up the kfuncs with proper lifetime annotations. This is useful for security and observability programs that need to capture argv/environment strings from exec events.

patches.title: bpf: tcp: Introduce bpf_tcp_ops.{enqueue,dequeue}_rcvq()
patches.author: Kuniyuki Iwashima
patches.summary: Second patch of a 7-patch series adding bpf_tcp_ops hooks for TCP AutoLOWAT. The series introduces enqueue/dequeue callbacks for the receive queue and a new kfunc to adjust sk->sk_rcvlowat dynamically from BPF, enabling userspace-transparent receive buffering policies. MPTCP support is explicitly excluded with a clear comment explaining the constraint.

patches.title: bpf: htab: Split htab_elem_lru and htab_elem_pcpu off of htab_elem
patches.author: T.J. Mercier
patches.summary: First patch of a 2-patch v5 series reducing BPF hash map memory consumption by splitting the LRU and per-CPU element variants into dedicated structs. The second patch uses the size reduction to shave 8 bytes off elem_size for maps with small keys, yielding meaningful memory savings at scale in production deployments.

patches.title: bpftool: Read ring buffer maps with event_pipe
patches.author: Tianyi Chen
patches.summary: First patch of a 2-patch v5 series adding event_pipe support to bpftool's ring buffer consumer. The patch lets bpftool stream ring buffer events into a named pipe, enabling integration with external log consumers. This fifth revision incorporates review feedback on pipe lifecycle and error handling, making the feature ready for upstream merge.

patches.title: selftests/bpf: keep headers off the generic link command line
patches.author: Mykola Lysenko
patches.summary: First patch of a 9-patch v8 series restructuring the selftests/bpf Makefile as a layered build. The series separates shared build variables into Makefile.buildvars, extracts BPF skeleton generation into a helper script, builds each test runner in its own sub-make, and derives the bench object list from sources automatically. This overhaul significantly improves incremental build times and parallelism for the BPF selftest suite.

patches.title: bpf: Destroy callee-local dynptrs on subprog return
patches.author: Xu Yunxiang
patches.summary: Part of a 2-patch v5 series fixing verifier lifetime tracking for subprogram-local dynptrs and iterator-owned BTF pointers. The patch synthesizes dynptr teardown on subprog return for callee-local dynptrs that were never explicitly released, preventing silent escapes from subprogram scope.

patches.title: bpf: Speed up htab hashing for u32/u64 keys
patches.author: Mykyta Yatsenko
patches.summary: Optimizes the BPF hash table lookup hot path for 32-bit and 64-bit integer keys by replacing the generic jhash path with a faster direct multiplication-based hash. At Meta, u32/u64 keyed hash maps are the dominant workload, and this specialization reduces lookup latency measurably on high-throughput paths.

patches.title: bpf: Report BPF_F_PREORDER in cgroup program queries
patches.author: Hui Su
patches.summary: First patch of a 3-patch series exposing the BPF_F_PREORDER cgroup attach flag through BPF_PROG_QUERY. Previously this flag was write-only, preventing userspace tools from auditing cgroup hook execution order. The series adds bpftool support for displaying the flag and a selftest to validate query results for preorder-attached programs.
